c.tagline: The ancient Inca capital, gateway to Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley.

taxi.fareNote: Cusco taxis are unmetered; agree the fare before getting in (short in-town rides run about S/5-10). Uber and InDrive have limited coverage, so most rides are hailed on the street or booked by phone.

emergency.note: 105 reaches the national police; 116/106 is for medical/ambulance (SAMU). Altitude sickness (soroche) is the most common traveler issue at 3,400 m - ascend slowly and hydrate.

avoid.reason: Petty theft around San Pedro market and nightlife; avoid walking alone at night in outer areas

hood_desc: The walkable heart of the city around the Plaza de Armas, ringed by the cathedral, colonial arcades, restaurants, and travel agencies; best for first-timers who want every major sight on their doorstep.

Cusco's bohemian artisan quarter of steep cobbled lanes, galleries, cafes, and viewpoints just uphill from the plaza; suits travelers after character, craft shops, and rooftop views (be ready for the climb at altitude).
A lively, local, budget-friendly area around the Eiffel-designed San Pedro Market, five minutes west of the plaza; good for food stalls, cheap eats, and easy transport connections.
One of Cusco's oldest and quietest neighborhoods, climbing west of the center to the 16th-century Santa Ana church and sweeping city views; full of affordable guesthouses and a residential feel.
A modern residential district with wider streets, shopping centers, local markets, and the closest access to the airport and bus terminals; a calmer, more authentic base away from the tourist core.

water.note: Drink bottled, boiled or filtered water; tap water is not safe for visitors.

transit.pay: Pay the flat fare in cash to the driver or fare collector on board - about S/1 (~$0.30) for a city combi ride. There is no rechargeable transit card; carry small coins.
transit.hours: Combis and colectivos run roughly 5am to 10-11pm; after that, taxis (agree the fare first) fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Cusco has no metro or tram; the compact historic center is best explored on foot, with combis and taxis covering longer trips and the outer districts.

train: PeruRail / Inca Rail to Ollantaytambo & Aguas Calientes (Machu Picchu)
bus: Combis & colectivos to the Sacred Valley

transit.m: Combi or colectivo from outside the terminal to the center, ~20-30 min
Taxi to Plaza de Armas, 15-25 min

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~10% at sit-down restaurants for good service is appreciated.
